blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior level, the mental habit of thinking in debits and credits does not disappear — it becomes invisible. Experienced accountants no longer consciously write 'DR' and 'CR'; they simply know, for any proposed change to the business, what the two sides are and whether they match. The habit becomes second nature, like reading without sounding out the letters.

This habit pays off exactly where it matters most: in meetings where somebody proposes an action that has one visible side and one invisible one. A price cut looks like a revenue decision; the experienced accountant notices the margin impact at the same second. A working capital improvement looks like cash; the experienced accountant notices what it does to receivables and customer relationships at the same time.

Had the team not thought in both sides, the decision would have been incomplete. The discipline is never obvious, and it is the difference between a finance partner who helps and one who merely records.

items.q: According to the text, what happens to debit/credit thinking at senior level?
options: It grows more explicit and formal
items.why: "it does not disappear — it becomes invisible"; vira segunda natureza, automático.

items.q: How does the text characterise a price cut?
options: As something with a visible revenue side and an invisible margin side
As a decision the accountant should avoid
items.why: "A price cut looks like a revenue decision; the experienced accountant notices the margin impact at the same second."

items.q: The reading-without-sounding-out-the-letters comparison is used to suggest that…
options: juniors should never learn the rules
the skill is impossible for most people to acquire
the discipline has become effortless and no longer needs conscious steps
senior accountants stop understanding the mechanics
items.why: Inferência: a analogia da leitura fluente ilustra um domínio tão internalizado que dispensa o passo consciente.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Many decisions carry a second side that is easy to miss.
The discipline is valuable precisely because it is not obvious.
Recording the numbers accurately is, by itself, the essence of senior finance.
A finance partner adds more value than someone who merely records.
items.why: Inferência: o texto contrapõe o parceiro que ajuda ao que só registra — registrar bem, sozinho, não é o ápice.

items.q: What does the conditional sentence "Had the team not thought in both sides, the decision would have been incomplete" imply?
options: The team ignored one of the sides and failed
Only one side ever matters in practice
The team did consider both sides, which is why the decision was sound
items.why: Inferência (conditional perfect): a frase é contrafactual — na realidade pensaram nos dois lados, então a decisão não ficou incompleta.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry fazendo o debrief de uma reunião com a diretoria. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, quick debrief on this morning's pricing session — because I think something worth noticing happened. The commercial team came in wanting to sign off on a nine percent cut on the core line. On paper, clean and simple: defend the volume, protect the account. Everyone in the room was nodding.

And then Priya, our finance partner, asked one quiet question. She said, fine — but what does this do to the other side? Because a nine percent cut on that line is not a revenue conversation, it is a margin conversation, and at our current cost base that wipes out roughly a third of the contribution. Nobody had run that number.

Now here is the part I want you to take away. She did not block the decision. She reframed it. Had she stayed silent, we would have walked out approving a cut that quietly gave away the profit we were trying to defend. Instead the CEO asked for the margin bridge, and the whole conversation changed in about ninety seconds.

That, to me, is the difference between someone who records what we decide and someone who actually partners with the business. I want more of that instinct in the team.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What did the commercial team want to do at the start of the session?
options: Raise prices on the core line
Sign off on a nine percent cut on the core line
items.why: "wanting to sign off on a nine percent cut on the core line."

items.q: What point did Priya raise about the proposed cut?
options: That the volume forecast was too optimistic
That the account should be dropped
That the cut was too small to matter
That it was really a margin conversation, not just a revenue one
items.why: "a nine percent cut on that line is not a revenue conversation, it is a margin conversation."

items.q: According to Harry, what would have happened had Priya stayed silent?
options: The CEO would have cancelled the product line
The meeting would have ended earlier
The team would have approved a cut that gave away the profit they were defending
items.why: "Had she stayed silent, we would have walked out approving a cut that quietly gave away the profit we were trying to defend."

items.q: What does Harry mean when he says Priya "did not block the decision. She reframed it"?
options: She rewrote the pricing model herself
She changed how the decision was understood rather than vetoing it
She asked to postpone the meeting
items.why: Inferência: reframe é mudar o enquadramento — ela não vetou, fez a sala ver o outro lado.

items.q: What is Harry's main takeaway for the team?
options: The team should stop cutting prices
He wants more of the instinct that catches the hidden second side
items.why: Inferência: ele elogia o instinto de Priya e diz "I want more of that instinct in the team" — partner vs. mero recorder.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "For a seasoned controller, spotting the offsetting entry has become second nature." This means it is…
options: something done automatically, without conscious effort
items.why: Second nature = segunda natureza: algo tão internalizado que sai sem esforço consciente.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "A discount defends volume, but its ___ can quietly erase the contribution you meant to protect."
items.why: Margin impact = impacto na margem — o efeito escondido de um corte de preço.

items.q: "She reads a proposal the way a fluent reader reads a page — no longer needing to sound out each rule." To sound out here means to…
options: work through something letter by letter, or step by step
items.why: To sound out (letters) = soletrar/decodificar passo a passo; aqui, metáfora para não precisar do passo consciente.

items.q: A finance partner, as opposed to a recorder, is best described as someone who…
options: owns a stake in the company
actively shapes and improves the decisions of the business
items.why: Finance partner = parceiro financeiro: ajuda a moldar a decisão, não apenas registra (record).

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Every proposal has a ___ side that anyone can see and an invisible side that only the trained eye catches."
items.why: Visible side = lado visível — contraposto ao invisible side que só o especialista percebe.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem à mesa da diretoria. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CEO still has to sign off on the revised pricing." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Before we commit, let's flag up the margin exposure to the board." To flag up means to…
items.why: Flag up = chamar a atenção para algo, sinalizar um ponto de risco.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the discount once they saw the contribution hit." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "She spotted the second side, but nobody followed through on building the margin bridge." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi identificado ou combinado.

items.q: "Trimming the price alone won't move the needle on profitability." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir diferença perceptível.
